question: What is the main goal of using direct nursing delivery technology in the hospital?

options.A: To increase the time spent on paper charting
options.B: To eliminate the need for physician rounds
options.C: To streamline bedside patient care and reduce errors
options.D: To replace human nurses with automated systems

explanation: You've got this! These tech tools are here to help you at the bedside, making care safer and easier without ever replacing your clinical judgment. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T3#GNS113_U4_T3_h1)

question: When bringing new bedside technology into the ward, what must nurses always balance it with?
explanation: Spot on! Technology is a great helper, but it should never come between the warm, caring connection you share with your patients. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T3#GNS113_U4_T3_h1)

question: During a Barcode Medication Administration check, which three things do you typically scan?

options.A: Patient wristband, medication package, and nurse badge
options.B: Patient chart, drug label, and infusion pump
options.C: Doctor prescription, bed number, and drug carton
options.D: Hospital card, clinic folder, and nurse badge

explanation: Great job! Scanning the patient, the drug, and yourself makes sure the right medication safely reaches the right person every single time. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T3#GNS113_U4_T3_h2)

question: How does Barcode Medication Administration mainly protect patients from mistakes?

options.A: By automatically calculating drug dosages for doctors
options.B: By diagnosing adverse drug reactions early
options.C: By ordering new drug supplies from the pharmacy
options.D: By establishing a closed-loop verification process

explanation: You're doing great! The system double-checks patient details against the digital prescription right before you give the drug, catching any mix-ups early. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T3#GNS113_U4_T3_h2)

question: What special safety feature does a smart IV pump have that older pumps lack?

options.A: A wireless connection to the national health database
options.C: A built-in blood pressure cuff monitor
options.D: A built-in drug library with dose error reduction limits

explanation: Awesome! The built-in drug library acts like a safety net, warning you if an infusion rate is set dangerously high or low. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T3#GNS113_U4_T3_h3)

question: Why are smart pumps so important when giving high-alert medications?

options.A: High-alert drugs change color inside intravenous tubing
options.B: Standard pumps cannot pump viscous fluid solutions
options.C: These medications must be infused within five seconds
options.D: Small programming errors can cause severe patient harm

explanation: Spot on! Because drugs like strong electrolytes have very narrow safe zones, smart pumps help us keep patients completely safe. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T3#GNS113_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the main job of a smart bed that has an exit alarm?

options.A: Detecting when a fall-risk patient attempts to get up
options.B: Weighing the patient during surgical procedures
options.C: Automatically adjusting room temperature for comfort
options.D: Administering pain medication when pressure increases

explanation: You've got this! Bed exit sensors sound an instant alert so we can rush over and stop a fall before it happens. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T3#GNS113_U4_T3_h4)

question: How do continuous patient monitoring devices make hospital wards safer?

options.A: Diagnosing complex medical conditions without doctor input
options.B: Removing the need to perform manual patient assessments
options.C: Replacing the physical presence of nurses in the ward
options.D: Detecting sudden clinical deterioration early through automated alerts

explanation: Brilliant! These tools catch tiny changes in vital signs long before a crisis shows up during routine rounds. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T3#GNS113_U4_T3_h4)

question: What do we call it when nurses get so used to constant, non-urgent machine alarms that they stop noticing them?
explanation: Spot on! When too many false beeps go off, it's easy to tune them out—which is why managing alarms safely is such a big deal in nursing. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T3#GNS113_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical workflow challenge when using clinical technology?

options.A: Cumbersome login procedures delaying urgent care
options.B: Frequent network failures and technical glitches
options.C: Instantaneous elimination of all charting errors
options.D: Desensitization caused by constant device noise

explanation: You nailed it! Technology helps us catch mistakes, but it doesn't magically wipe out all errors overnight—new tools often bring their own little hurdles! [learn more](GNS113_U4_T3#GNS113_U4_T3_h5)
